text:
Collin Graf hasn't had a point in nine games, and San Jose Hockey Now's headline says what he thinks of it: not happy with his start, trying to stay positive. The undrafted Quinnipiac winger, who scored 26 goals in his first 121 NHL games, has three points in 20 this season.

Half of it is luck. Two goals on 4.29 expected goals (the quality of his chances) is a real shortfall, and our numbers flag him as due. The other half is that the chances have thinned during the drought, so it isn't all bounces. The Sharks are out-chanced with him on the ice at five on five (47%), though that's better than the team without him. Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.2 wins above replacement last season, 132nd of 401 forwards, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had more than half his shots coming off the rush. Ryan Warsofsky still trusts him: Sharks Hockey Digest's Max Miller noted Graf on the ice with Macklin Celebrini at the end of a tight third period on Nov. 9. Our projection has him back near 14 goals.
